Why Slow Reading Wins

Notes on attention, e-ink and the pleasures of friction

There is a particular pleasure in reading slowly. Not the forced slowness of a difficult text, but the chosen slowness of a long afternoon & a device that refuses to ping you.

Thanks for reading The Quiet Desk! Subscribe for free.

Friction is a feature

E-ink screens are slow to refresh. Page turns take a beat. That beat matters: it gives the eye a moment to rest, and the mind a moment to consolidate.

“We read to know we are not alone.” — attributed, dubiously, to C. S. Lewis

Multilingual margins

Readers write to me in many scripts: 日本語の読者、Ελληνικοί αναγνώστες, and the occasional emoji 📚. Unicode should survive the trip to the device — including “curly quotes”, en–dashes, and the ellipsis…

  • Short lists help.
  • So do code spans and strikethrough.
  1. Lists can start anywhere.
const pages = read(slowly);
if (pages > 10) rest();
